text.p: Minuteman International Inc said Monday it expects sales in the second half of 1997 to continue to be strong, although profits will be constrained by investments for the future.
Jerome Rau, president, said sales in the second half will be bolstered by additional product introductions and ongoing improvements at the chemicals division.

"Even though profits will be restricted due to investments for the long-term, we remain committed to our growth strategy so that we can continue as the front runner in this industry," Rau said in a statement.
Earlier, Minuteman reported second quarter earnings of $0.24, up from $0.23 a year ago. Sales were $14.0 million, up from $12.1 million a year ago.
General and administrative expenses in the quarter rose 24 percent to $2.5 million, while the cost of sales rose 15.4 percent to $9.4 million.
Minuteman makes commercial and industrial vacuums and floor and carpet care equipment, chemical cleaning and coating products, and litter pick-up machines and lawn sweeping equipment.
